question.text: An exporter shorts 300 lots of USDINR futures at 84.00 to hedge USD 300,000 receivable. At expiry, spot (FBIL) rate is 85.50. What is the effective realization rate?

explanation.text: The Logic: The exporter sells USD in the spot/FBIL market at 85.50 and loses 1.50 on the short futures position entered at 84.00 because final settlement is against the FBIL rate. Spot sale: 300,000 x 85.50 = Rs. 2,56,50,000. Futures loss: 300 x 1000 x (85.50 - 84.00) = Rs. 4,50,000. Net inflow: Rs. 2,52,00,000 / 300,000 = Rs. 84.00 per USD. The Trap: Without a hedge the exporter would realise Rs. 85.50; the hedge gives certainty by locking in 84.00 but gives up the favourable spot move. Note: The effective rate equals the futures entry price here only because the hedged amount and the final settlement reference (FBIL on the last trading day) match the underlying exposure exactly; any mismatch in size or timing breaks this clean result.
